Subject: Caching assumptions for pricing - follow-up & next steps

Thanks for the time today - quick recap and next steps from our side. Short version: we want to align on the traffic & caching assumptions so we can finalize unit pricing scenarios.

Call highlights / what we heard:
- Expected production traffic: ~8M requests/month (rough estimate from your team).
- Average tokens per request: ~90 tokens (prompt) + ~60 tokens (completion) = ~150 tokens/request.
- Monthly token estimate (prompt + completion): ~1.2B tokens/month.
- You mentioned ~30-45% of traffic likely re-uses a small set of prompt templates/prefixes (lots of templated product queries + the same system prompt). This is the part we can prefix-cache.

Questions / assumptions to confirm:
1) Can you confirm the 8M reqs/month and the 90/60 token split, or share the sample CSV you mentioned? (we attached postcall_volume_estimates.xlsx)
2) For prefix caching: are canonical prefixes stable for >24 hours or do they change per-user? (affects TTL choice)
3) What is your target effective price per 1M tokens (after caching)? You mentioned wanting to be in the low-mid hundreds - we want the exact target to validate scenarios.

What we'll do next (from Redwood):
- Marcus will model unit economics across hit rates (20/40/60%) and share an XLS with scenarios showing raw compute cost, effective cost after cache, and recommended pricing targets.
- We'll outline a short instrumentation plan (2-week pilot) to measure cache hit rate and sample prompts.

Attachments: postcall_volume_estimates.xlsx (your sheet + prompt samples you can fill in)

Thanks - I'll follow up with Marcus's scenario sheet and proposed pilot steps by EOD tomorrow.

—

Thanks Marissa - quick confirmations from our side:
- The 8M requests/month estimate is our current target for Q3; could spike to ~12M if adoption is faster.
- Token split: our instrumented logs put the average prompt at ~90 tokens and completion at ~60 tokens (so ~150 tokens total/request is a good working number).
- On prefix cacheability: around 30-45% of requests hit a small set of templates (search-style queries and product-detail prompts). These prefixes are fairly stable for 24-72 hours; some user-specific tokens are appended after the prefix.

Target pricing: we're aiming for an effective cost (after caching) of roughly $250–$350 per 1M tokens from a procurement standpoint. If you can show scenarios where we hit that band with realistic cache hit rates, we can move to pilot + SOW.

We filled the sample CSV with a subset of prompts (attached to my reply). Let me know if you want more.

Subject: Re: Caching assumptions for pricing - follow-up & next steps

Thanks Jared - appreciate the clarifications. I ran three quick scenarios to show how effective $/1M tokens changes with hit rate and a couple of knobs we control. High-level notes first, then the numbers.

High-level pricing model (simplified):
- "Raw compute cost" = our estimated cost to execute the model on your workload, expressed per 1M tokens processed by the model (prompt + completion). This includes GPU cycles, memory, and runtime overhead.
- "Cache hit rate" (prefix cache) reduces the number of tokens that need full model inference. We assume full hits avoid the completion compute; partial/short-circuit cache behavior depends on the prefix length.
- "Effective billed tokens" = billed_tokens = total_tokens * (1 - hit_rate)  (we model that a hit avoids ~100% of the tokens for that request's inference).

Assumptions used in the sheet I attached:
- Baseline raw compute cost: $1,200 per 1M tokens (model variant selected for quality/latency).
- Platform & infra overhead + support margin: +25% applied to raw compute for list price scenarios.
- Proposed Redwood list price (no commit) ~ $1,500 per 1M tokens (this is illustrative; enterprise committed pricing will be lower).

Scenario table (effective cost per 1M tokens after cache):
- 20% hit rate: effective compute cost = 1,200 * (1 - 0.20) = $960 -> +25% overhead = $1,200 effective price per 1M
- 40% hit rate: effective compute cost = 1,200 * (1 - 0.40) = $720 -> +25% overhead = $900 effective price per 1M
- 60% hit rate: effective compute cost = 1,200 * (1 - 0.60) = $480 -> +25% overhead = $600 effective price per 1M

Compare to your target ($250–$350 per 1M): with the above baseline model, you'd need an unrealistically high cache hit (~85-90%) or a different model/quantization profile to get down to $300/1M. Options to get into your band:
- Increase cache coverage (prefix engineering, stronger canonicalization) — aim for 70%+ hit rate (depends on UX & how many user-specific tokens are appended).
- Use a lower-cost model family (quantized variant) where raw compute is ~$300–500 per 1M tokens; with 40% hit that can hit your target. We can validate quality tradeoffs with a small eval set.
- Commit to reserved capacity (Dedicated) for volume discounts — committed pricing can be 2–3x cheaper than list depending on an annual/monthly commit and burst allowances.

Pilot proposal (next steps we recommend):
1) 2-week instrumented pilot where we log per-request: canonicalized-prefix-id, is_cache_hit, request_tokens, response_tokens.
2) We (Redwood) will enable prefix caching with a 24h TTL initially and run with your sample traffic or a shadow run.
3) After 2 weeks we'll compute observed hit rate, update the pricing scenario sheet, and propose 1–2 pricing decks: (A) Dedicated commit with quantized model + cache optimization, (B) Hosted + high cache engineering.

I attached pricing_scenarios_v2.xlsx with the detailed calculations and a quick sensitivity table. If you want, Aditya can scope the instrumentation steps and the small config changes to enable prefix keys.

—

Thanks Marcus - that is very helpful and lines up with our instincts. Quick reply:
- Let's proceed with the 2-week pilot (instrumented) focusing on the product-detail & search prompts — those are the highest volume templates.
- We'll prioritize canonicalizing prefixes on our side to try to boost hit-rate.
- Target for pilot: observe real hit rate and aim for a path to an effective $/1M in the $250–$350 range via either cache improvements + quantized model + committed capacity.

Please send SOW/short pilot plan and we'll loop in procurement. Happy to do a quick kickoff tomorrow.
